column9: Lie flat on a bench with your feet flat on the ground and your back pressed against the bench.|Grasp the barbell with an overhand grip slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.|Lift the barbell off the rack and hold it directly above your chest with your arms fully extended.|Lower the barbell slowly towards your chest, keeping your elbows tucked in.|Pause for a moment when the barbell touches your chest.

Lie flat on a bench with your feet flat on the ground and your back pressed against the bench.|Hold a dumbbell in each hand, with your palms facing forward and your arms extended above your chest.|Lower the dumbbells slowly to the sides of your chest, keeping your elbows at a 90-degree angle.|Pause for a moment, then push the dumbbells back up to the starting position, fully extending your arms.|Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Start in a high plank position with your hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart and your feet together.|Engage your core and lower your body towards the ground by bending your elbows, keeping your body in a straight line.|Pause for a moment when your chest is just above the ground, then push yourself back up to the starting position by straightening your arms.|Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand at shoulder level with your palms facing forward.|Press the dumbbells upward until your arms are fully extended overhead.|Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower the dumbbells back down to shoulder level.|Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and hold a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing your body.|Keep your back straight and engage your core.|Raise your arms out to the sides until they are parallel to the floor, keeping a slight bend in your elbows.|Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your arms back down to the starting position.|Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell vertically against your chest with both hands.|Keeping your chest up and core engaged, lower your body down into a squat position by pushing your hips back and bending your knees.|Continue lowering until your thighs are parallel to the ground, or as low as you can comfortably go.|Pause for a moment at the bottom, then push through your heels to return to the starting position.|Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Sit in the leg press with your back flat against the pad.|Place your feet shoulder-width apart in the middle of the platform.|Release the safety handles and lower the platform until your knees are bent to about 90 degrees.|Push the platform away through your heels until your legs are almost straight.|Stop short of locking your knees and lower again under control.

Stand up straight with your feet shoulder-width apart and hold a barbell with an underhand grip, palms facing forward.|Keep your elbows close to your torso and exhale as you curl the weights while contracting your biceps.|Continue to raise the bar until your biceps are fully contracted and the bar is at shoulder level.|Hold the contracted position for a brief pause as you squeeze your biceps.|Inhale as you slowly begin to lower the bar back to the starting position.

Sit on the edge of a bench or chair with your hands gripping the edge, fingers pointing forward.|Slide your butt off the bench, supporting your weight with your hands.|Bend your elbows and lower your body towards the ground, keeping your back close to the bench.|Pause for a moment at the bottom, then push yourself back up to the starting position.|Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Hang from a pull-up bar with your arms fully extended and your palms facing away from you.|Engage your core and lift your legs up in front of you, keeping them straight.|Continue lifting until your legs are parallel to the ground or slightly higher.|Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your legs back down to the starting position.|Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Set a rope attachment on a cable pulley just above head height.|Grab an end of the rope in each hand with your thumbs pointing back.|Step back until your arms are straight and the weight is off the stack.|Pull the rope towards your forehead, splitting your hands apart as you go.|Hold the squeeze between your shoulder blades and return under control.

Step onto a box so your chin already clears the bar.|Grab the bar with your palms facing away from you.|Take your feet off the box and hold the top position.|Lower yourself as slowly as you can, counting to three.|Step back up to the top and start the next rep.

Lie face down with your arms stretched out in front of you.|Keep your neck in line with your spine.|Lift your arms, chest and legs off the floor at the same time.|Squeeze your glutes and lower back at the top.|Lower everything back down slowly and repeat.

Put your hands on a bench or a sturdy box, slightly wider than your shoulders.|Walk your feet back until your body is in a straight line.|Lower your chest to the edge of the bench.|Keep your elbows at about forty-five degrees from your body.|Push back up until your arms are straight.

Lie on your back with your arms up and your knees over your hips.|Press your lower back into the floor.|Lower one arm overhead and the opposite leg towards the floor.|Stop just before your back arches and come back to the start.|Alternate sides on every rep.

Get on all fours with your hands under your shoulders and knees under your hips.|Keep your back flat and your neck in line with your spine.|Reach one arm forward and the opposite leg back at the same time.|Hold for a second without letting your hips tilt.|Return to all fours and swap sides.

Anchor a band at chest height and stand side-on to it.|Hold the band with both hands against your sternum.|Step away until the band pulls hard to the side.|Press your hands straight forward without rotating.|Bring them back to your chest and keep your hips still.

Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart.|Lower your body by bending your knees and pushing your hips back as if sitting on a chair.|Keep your chest up and your back straight.|Lower yourself until your thighs are parallel to the ground.|Push through your heels to return to the starting position.

Stand with your back flat against a wall and your feet a step forward.|Slide down until your knees are bent at ninety degrees.|Keep your knees over your ankles and your back on the wall.|Rest your hands on your thighs or hold them out in front.|Hold the position until your legs give in.

Stand with your feet hip-width apart and a dumbbell in each hand in front of your thighs.|Keep a soft bend in your knees and your back flat.|Push your hips back and slide the dumbbells down your legs.|Stop when you feel a stretch along the back of your thighs.|Squeeze your glutes to bring your hips forward and stand tall.

Sit on the floor with your upper back against a bench and a barbell over your hips.|Plant your feet flat, about hip-width apart and under your knees.|Tuck your chin and drive through your heels to lift your hips.|Squeeze your glutes hard when your body forms a straight line.|Lower your hips slowly until they nearly touch the floor.

Lie on your back with your knees bent and your feet flat on the floor.|Rest your arms at your sides with your palms down.|Push through your heels to lift your hips off the floor.|Squeeze your glutes until your body forms a straight line.|Lower your hips back down slowly, one vertebra at a time.

Lie face down on the machine with your hips at the edge of the pad.|Hold the handles and let your legs hang down.|Squeeze your glutes to lift your legs until they are level with your back.|Avoid arching your lower back at the top.|Lower your legs slowly and do not let them swing.

Set your forearms on the floor, elbows under your shoulders.|Step your feet back until your body is one straight line from head to heels.|Squeeze your glutes and brace your abs.|Keep your hips level, neither sagging nor piked up.|Breathe steadily and hold for the time you set.

Grab a pull-up bar with an overhand grip, hands shoulder-width apart.|Lift your feet and hang with straight arms.|Let your shoulders stretch while keeping a light brace in your abs.|Hold for the time you set, then step down under control.

Adjust the backrest and ensure the machine axis of rotation aligns directly with the lateral side of your knee joint.|Grasp the side handles firmly, pull yourself down into the seat, and engage your core to lock your hips and pelvis in place.|Exhale as you extend your legs upward in a smooth, controlled motion by contracting your quadriceps.|Hold the fully extended position for 1–2 seconds at the top of the movement.|Inhale as you slowly lower the weight back to the starting position over a 2- to 3-second cadence.

Jump or step up to the top of the dip bars with straight arms.|Pull your shoulders down and keep your chest slightly forward.|Bend your elbows and lower yourself as slowly as you can, counting to three.|Stop when your shoulders drop below your elbows.|Step back up to the top and start the next rep.

Stand tall with your feet hip-width apart and your hands on your thighs.|Keep a soft bend in your knees and your back flat.|Push your hips back and slide your hands down your legs.|Stop when you feel a stretch along the back of your thighs.|Squeeze your glutes to bring your hips back under you.

Set a bar at about waist height, or use the edge of a sturdy table.|Take an overhand grip a little wider than your shoulders.|Walk your feet forward so your body hangs at an angle, straight from head to heels.|Pull your chest to the bar and squeeze your shoulder blades together.|Lower yourself under control until your arms are straight.

Hold a door frame, a pole or a suspension strap at arm length.|Stand with your feet a little wider than your shoulders.|Sit back and down, using your hands only as much as you need.|Go as deep as you can while keeping your heels on the floor.|Drive through your whole foot to stand back up.

Loop a band above your knees and lie on your side.|Bend your knees and stack your feet.|Open the top knee against the band without rolling your hips.|Hold for a second at the top.|Close the knee slowly and keep the tension.

Grab a pull-up bar with your hands shoulder-width apart.|Hang with your arms straight and your feet off the floor.|Pull your shoulders down and away from your ears.|Keep your ribs down and your body still.|Hold the position for as long as your grip lets you.

Adjust the machine to your desired height and secure your knees on the pad.|Grasp the handles with your palms facing down and your arms fully extended.|Lower your body by bending your elbows until your upper arms are parallel to the floor.|Pause for a moment, then push yourself back up to the starting position.|Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Anchor a band behind your head and lie on your back.|Hold the band with straight arms over your chest.|Lift your knees to ninety degrees over your hips.|Lower one leg towards the floor while your arms hold the band.|Swap legs and keep your lower back flat throughout.

Anchor a band to a post at chest height and hold one end in each hand.|Step back until the band is tight with your arms straight in front of you.|Keep a slight bend in your elbows and your knees soft.|Open your arms out to the sides until they line up with your shoulders.|Bring your hands back together in front of your chest slowly.

column2: Barbell Lying Back of the Head Tricep Extension
column9: Lie flat on a bench with your feet flat on the ground and your head at the end of the bench.|Hold a barbell with an overhand grip, hands shoulder-width apart, and extend your arms straight up over your chest.|Keeping your upper arms stationary, slowly lower the barbell behind your head by bending your elbows.|Pause for a moment, then extend your arms back up to the starting position.|Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Stand on the middle of a band and hold one end in each hand.|Keep your feet shoulder-width apart and your palms facing forward.|Curl one hand up towards your shoulder while the other stays down.|Lower it and curl the other hand in turn.|Keep your elbows still and speed up once the motion feels easy.

Stand with the balls of your feet on the middle of a band.|Hold the ends of the band up at your shoulders.|Rise up onto your toes as high as you can.|Pause at the top and squeeze your calves.|Lower your heels slowly back to the floor.

Lie on your back with your knees bent and your feet flat on the floor.|Place your hands lightly beside your head.|Curl up and twist to bring one elbow towards the opposite knee.|Squeeze your abs as the elbow and knee meet.|Lower back down and repeat on the other side.

Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and hold a barbell in front of you with an overhand grip.|Keep your arms straight and your back straight throughout the exercise.|Lift your shoulders up towards your ears as high as possible, squeezing your traps at the top.|Hold for a moment, then slowly lower your shoulders back down to the starting position.|Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Sit on a bench with your feet flat on the ground and hold a barbell with an overhand grip, palms facing down.|Rest your forearms on your thighs, allowing your wrists to hang off the edge.|Slowly curl your wrists upward, bringing the barbell towards your body.|Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower the barbell back down to the starting position.|Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Set the back extension bench so the pad sits just below your hips.|Hook your ankles under the foot pads and cross your arms over your chest.|Lower your upper body slowly by bending at the hips.|Raise your torso back up until your body forms a straight line.|Squeeze your glutes at the top without arching your lower back.

Loop a band above your knees and stand shoulder-width apart.|Push your knees out so the band stays tight.|Sit back and down into a squat.|Keep your chest up and your knees tracking over your toes.|Drive through your feet to stand back up.

Loop a band around one foot and hold the other end under your hands.|Get on all fours with your back flat.|Push the banded foot up towards the ceiling with the knee bent.|Squeeze the glute at the top of the kick.|Bring the knee back down slowly against the band.

Hang from a pull-up bar with your palms facing away from you.|Pull your shoulders down and away from your ears.|Squeeze your glutes and push your chest through so your body forms an arch.|Look forward and keep your legs straight and together.|Hold the arch for as long as the routine asks for.

Anchor a band to a post at chest height and face away from it.|Hold one end in each hand with your arms open to the sides.|Step forward until the band is tight.|Bring your hands together in front of your chest with a slight bend in the elbows.|Hold for a moment and open your arms back out slowly.

Stand on the middle of a band and hold one end in each hand.|Keep your back straight and your abs drawn in.|Pull your hands up towards your collarbone, lifting your elbows out wide.|Stop when your elbows are level with your shoulders.|Lower your hands slowly back to your thighs.

Lie flat on a bench with your feet flat on the ground and your head at the end of the bench.|Hold the barbell with an overhand grip, hands shoulder-width apart, and extend your arms straight up over your chest.|Keeping your upper arms stationary, slowly lower the barbell towards your forehead by bending your elbows.|Pause for a moment at the bottom, then extend your arms back up to the starting position.|Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Sit on a bench with your feet flat on the floor and a barbell resting on your thighs.|Place the balls of your feet on a raised platform, such as a block or step.|Position the barbell across your thighs and hold it securely with your hands.|Keeping your back straight and your core engaged, lift your heels off the ground by extending your ankles.|Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your heels back down to the starting position.

Sit on the floor with one leg straight and the other tucked in.|Keep your back long instead of rounding it.|Hinge forward over the straight leg.|Reach towards your foot until you feel the hamstring pull.|Hold the stretch, then change legs.

Stand tall with a kettlebell hanging in one hand.|Put your free hand behind your head and keep your hips square.|Bend sideways towards the loaded side, letting the bell slide down your leg.|Come back up by pulling with the opposite side of your waist.|Finish the set, then swap hands.

Stand facing the cable machine with your feet shoulder-width apart.|Grasp the cable handles with an overhand grip and let your arms hang down in front of you.|Keeping your arms straight, shrug your shoulders up towards your ears.|Hold the contraction for a moment, then slowly lower your shoulders back down to the starting position.|Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Sit on a bench with your feet flat on the ground and your forearms resting on your thighs, holding a barbell with an underhand grip.|Allow the barbell to roll down to your fingertips, keeping your wrists straight.|Slowly curl the barbell up towards your forearms by flexing your wrists.|Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower the barbell back down to the starting position.|Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Attach the ankle cuff to your ankle and stand facing the cable machine.|Position yourself far enough away from the machine so that there is tension on the cable.|Place your hands on the machine for support.|Keeping your leg straight, slowly move your leg across your body towards the midline.|Pause for a moment at the end of the movement, then slowly return to the starting position.

Loop a band above your knees and get on all fours.|Keep your hips level and your back flat.|Lift one knee out to the side against the band.|Do not let your torso lean to the other side.|Lower the knee slowly and keep the band under tension.

Adjust the machine to your desired weight and height settings.|Grasp the handles with an overhand grip, slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.|Hang with your arms fully extended and your feet off the ground.|Engage your back muscles and pull your body up towards the handles, keeping your elbows close to your body.|Continue pulling until your chin is above the handles.

Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and hold a barbell with an overhand grip, palms facing down.|Keep your arms straight and raise the barbell in front of you until it reaches shoulder height.|Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower the barbell back down to the starting position.|Next, lower the barbell behind your head, keeping your arms straight.|Pause for a moment at the bottom, then raise the barbell back up to the starting position.

Get on all fours with your hands under your shoulders and knees under your hips.|Tuck your toes and lift your knees a couple of centimetres off the floor.|Keep your back flat and your shoulders over your hands.|Push the floor away and hold the position.|Breathe steadily and do not let your hips rise.

Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and grasp the cable handle with an overhand grip.|Keep your back straight and your core engaged.|Raise the cable handle in front of you, keeping your arms straight and your palms facing down.|Continue lifting until your arms are parallel to the floor.|Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower the cable handle back to the starting position.

Sit on a bench or chair with your knees bent and feet flat on the ground.|Hold the cable handle with your right hand and place your elbow on the inside of your right knee.|Extend your arm fully, keeping your elbow stationary and close to your knee.|Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your arm back to the starting position.|Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch sides.

Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and hold a barbell with an underhand grip, palms facing up.|Let the barbell hang at arm's length in front of your thighs.|Keeping your upper arms stationary, curl the barbell up towards your chest by contracting your biceps.|Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower the barbell back down to the starting position.|Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and place a barbell across your upper back.|Raise your heels off the ground as high as possible, using only your toes.|Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your heels back down to the starting position.|Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Stand with your feet hip-width apart holding a kettlebell in both hands.|Keep a small bend in your knees and your back flat.|Push your hips back and let the kettlebell slide down your legs.|Stop when you feel a stretch in your hamstrings.|Drive your hips forward to stand back up.

Lie on your side with your elbow under your shoulder and your legs stacked.|Lift your hips until your body forms a straight line.|Keep your top hip stacked over the bottom one without rolling forward.|Hold, breathing steadily, then switch sides.

Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and hold a dumbbell in each hand with your palms facing your body.|Keep your arms straight and let the dumbbells hang by your sides.|Raise your shoulders as high as possible, as if you are trying to touch your ears with your shoulders.|Hold the contraction for a second, then slowly lower your shoulders back down to the starting position.|Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Lie face down with your arms reaching forward.|Lift your arms, chest and legs off the floor.|Hold that position and breathe normally.|Keep your gaze down so your neck stays neutral.|Come back down once you cannot hold the shape.

Stand tall holding a dumbbell in each hand.|Take a wide step out to one side.|Push your hips back and bend that knee while the other leg stays straight.|Keep both feet flat and your chest up.|Push off the bent leg to return to the middle.

Loop a band above your knees and lie on your back.|Put the soles of your feet together and let your knees fall open.|Press your knees out against the band.|Squeeze your glutes to lift your hips off the floor.|Lower under control and go straight into the next rep.

Adjust the machine to your desired assistance level.|Stand on the foot platform and grip the handles with an overhand grip, slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.|Keep your chest up and shoulders back, engage your core, and slightly bend your knees.|Pull your body up by flexing your elbows and driving your elbows down towards your sides.|Continue pulling until your chin is above the bar.

Adjust the cable pulleys to chest height.|Stand in the center of the cable machine with one foot in front of the other.|Grasp the handles with your palms facing down and your arms extended out to the sides.|Take a step forward, keeping your arms slightly bent.|With a slight bend in your elbows, bring your hands together in front of your chest.

Lie on a flat bench with your legs hanging off the end from the knees down.|Hold the sides of the bench behind your head or tuck your hands under your hips.|Lift your legs a few centimetres off the bench with your feet together.|Raise your straight legs until they are almost vertical.|Lower them slowly without letting them touch the bench.

Sit on the floor side-on to a low pulley with your legs out in front.|Hold the handle with the arm nearest the stack, elbow bent at 90 degrees.|Keep your elbow tucked against your side the whole time.|Rotate your forearm across your stomach without moving the elbow.|Let the handle return slowly and switch sides after the set.

Adjust the cable machine to a low pulley position.|Attach a straight bar to the cable.|Stand facing away from the machine with your feet shoulder-width apart.|Grasp the bar with an overhand grip and extend your arms straight overhead.|Lean forward slightly, keeping your back straight and core engaged.

Sit on a preacher bench with your upper arms resting on the pad and your chest against the support.|Grasp the barbell with an underhand grip, slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.|Keeping your upper arms stationary, exhale and curl the barbell up towards your shoulders.|Pause for a moment at the top, squeezing your biceps.|Inhale and slowly lower the barbell back down to the starting position.

column2: Barbell Standing Rocking Leg Calf Raise
column9: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and hold a barbell across your upper back.|Raise your heels off the ground as high as possible, balancing on the balls of your feet.|Slowly lower your heels back down to the starting position.|Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Lie face down on the leg curl machine with the pad just above your heels.|Line your knees up with the machine's pivot and hold the handles.|Curl your heels towards your glutes as far as you can.|Squeeze your hamstrings at the top without lifting your hips.|Lower the pad slowly until your legs are almost straight.

Anchor a band high and stand side-on with your feet apart.|Hold the band with both hands above the far shoulder.|Pull it down and across your body towards the opposite hip.|Rotate through your torso and let your back foot pivot.|Return along the same path under control.

Stand tall holding a kettlebell in each hand at your sides.|Keep your arms straight and your chin tucked.|Lift your shoulders straight up towards your ears.|Pause at the top without rolling the shoulders.|Lower them slowly all the way down.

Pick up a heavy kettlebell in each hand and stand tall.|Pull your shoulders back and brace your core.|Walk in a straight line with short, controlled steps.|Do not let your torso lean or the bells swing.|Set them down when your grip starts to give out.

Stand with your feet slightly wider than your shoulders and a dumbbell in each hand.|Let the dumbbells hang at your sides with your arms straight.|Sit your hips back and bend your knees as if sitting on a chair.|Go down as far as you can while keeping your heels on the floor.|Drive through your heels to stand back up.

Loop a short band just above your knees.|Lie on your back with your knees bent and your feet flat.|Push your knees out against the band.|Drive through your heels to lift your hips.|Squeeze your glutes at the top and lower slowly.

Hold a band with both hands at shoulder width in front of your chest.|Keep your arms straight and your shoulders down.|Pull the band apart until your arms are out to the sides.|Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the end.|Bring your hands back together slowly.

Adjust the cable machine to a low position and attach the handles.|Sit on an incline bench with your back against the pad and feet flat on the floor.|Grasp the handles with an overhand grip and extend your arms straight out in front of you.|Keeping a slight bend in your elbows, open your arms out to the sides in a controlled motion.|Pause for a moment at the fully extended position, then slowly return to the starting position.

Lie on your back with your hands lightly behind your head.|Lift your shoulders off the floor and bring your knees up.|Bring one elbow towards the opposite knee as you extend the other leg.|Switch sides in a slow, controlled pedalling motion.|Keep your lower back pressed into the floor throughout.

Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and grasp the cable handles with an overhand grip.|Keep your arms straight and your core engaged.|Raise your arms out to the sides until they are parallel to the floor.|Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your arms back down to the starting position.|Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Attach a rope to a cable machine at a high position.|Stand facing away from the machine with your feet shoulder-width apart.|Grasp the rope with both hands, palms facing each other, and bring your hands above your head.|Keep your upper arms close to your head and your elbows pointing forward.|Slowly lower the rope behind your head by bending your elbows.

Set up an incline bench at a 45-degree angle.|Lie face down on the bench with your chest and stomach resting against it.|Hold a barbell with an underhand grip, shoulder-width apart.|Extend your arms fully, allowing the barbell to hang down towards the floor.|Keeping your upper arms stationary, exhale and curl the weights while contracting your biceps.

Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, toes pointing forward.|Place your hands on a wall or stable surface for balance.|Slowly raise your heels off the ground, lifting your body weight onto the balls of your feet.|Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your heels back down to the starting position.|Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Sit on the floor with both legs straight in front of you.|Sit up tall on your sit bones.|Hinge from your hips and reach towards your feet.|Let your head and neck relax as you fold.|Hold and breathe into the stretch.

Stand up straight with your feet shoulder-width apart and hold a dumbbell in one hand, letting it hang down by your side.|Keeping your back straight and your core engaged, slowly bend sideways at the waist towards the opposite side of the dumbbell, lowering the weight as far as you comfortably can.|Pause for a moment, then slowly return to the starting position.|Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch sides and repeat.

Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and your knees slightly bent.|Grasp the barbell with an overhand grip, hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.|Keep your arms straight and your shoulders relaxed.|Lift your shoulders up towards your ears, squeezing your traps at the top.|Hold for a moment, then slowly lower your shoulders back down to the starting position.

Kneel with your palms flat on the floor and your fingers pointing forward.|Rock your weight gently forward and back to open the front of your wrists.|Turn your hands so the fingers point back towards your knees and rock again.|Flip onto the backs of your hands and press down lightly.|Finish with slow fist circles in both directions to warm the joint.

Step onto the pedals and take hold of the moving handles.|Stand tall with your weight through the middle of your feet.|Push the pedals around in a smooth oval path.|Work the arms and legs together instead of just coasting.|Lower the resistance for the final minutes.

Sit with your upper back on a bench and a band around your hips.|Anchor both ends of the band under your feet or to the rack.|Push your hips up against the band's pull.|Squeeze your glutes when your body is level.|Lower your hips slowly without losing the tension.

Anchor a band at head height and hold an end in each hand.|Step back until the band is under tension.|Pull your hands towards your face, splitting them apart.|Keep your elbows high and squeeze your upper back.|Return your arms forward under control.

Adjust the seat so the handles line up with your lower chest.|Sit with your back against the pad and grab both handles.|Press the handles forward and down until your arms are almost straight.|Stop just short of locking your elbows.|Let the handles come back slowly to your chest.

Set both pulleys at shoulder height and stand in the middle of the station.|Take the left handle in your right hand and the right handle in your left, so the cables cross.|Hold your arms out in front of you with a slight bend in the elbows.|Pull your arms out and back until they line up with your shoulders.|Let your arms come back together in front of you slowly.

Attach a straight bar to a high pulley cable machine.|Stand facing the machine with your feet shoulder-width apart and a slight bend in your knees.|Grasp the bar with an overhand grip, hands shoulder-width apart.|Keep your elbows close to your sides and your upper arms stationary.|Exhale and push the bar down until your elbows are fully extended.

Stand up straight with your feet shoulder-width apart and hold a barbell with an overhand grip, palms facing down.|Keep your upper arms stationary and exhale as you curl the barbell upward, contracting your biceps.|Continue to raise the barbell until your biceps are fully contracted and the barbell is at shoulder level.|Hold the contracted position for a brief pause as you squeeze your biceps.|Inhale as you slowly lower the barbell back to the starting position, keeping your upper arms stationary.

Stand with your toes on an elevated surface, such as a step or block.|Place your hands on a stable support, such as a wall or railing, for balance.|Raise your heels as high as possible, lifting your body weight onto the balls of your feet.|Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your heels back down to the starting position.|Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Sit in the machine with the pad resting on your lower shins.|Lock the thigh pad down so your legs cannot lift.|Hold the handles and keep your back against the seat.|Curl your heels down and back as far as they go.|Let your legs straighten slowly against the resistance.

Sit on the floor with your knees bent and heels lightly down.|Hold the kettlebell by the horns in front of your chest.|Lean back slightly and lift your chest.|Rotate your torso to take the bell beside one hip, then the other.|Move from the ribs, not just the arms.

Start by standing with your feet shoulder-width apart and your arms extended in front of you.|Bend your knees slightly and hinge forward at the hips, keeping your back straight.|Lower your body by bending your elbows and retracting your shoulder blades, as if you are trying to squeeze a pencil between them.|Pause for a moment at the bottom, then push through your hands to extend your elbows and return to the starting position.|Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Step into the hack squat machine with your back and shoulders against the pads.|Place your feet shoulder-width apart in the middle of the platform.|Release the safety handles and bend your knees to lower yourself.|Go down until your thighs are about parallel to the platform.|Push through your heels to straighten your legs without locking your knees.

Anchor a band low and loop the free end around one ankle.|Stand facing the anchor and hold something for balance.|Kick the banded leg straight back, keeping it long.|Squeeze your glute at the end of the kick.|Bring the leg forward slowly against the band.

Anchor a band above your head and kneel underneath it.|Hold an end of the band in each hand with your arms overhead.|Pull your shoulder blades down first.|Bring your hands down to shoulder level, opening your chest.|Let your arms rise back up slowly.

Stand in a doorway and put a forearm on the frame.|Set your elbow at about shoulder height.|Step forward with the same-side foot until you feel the stretch.|Keep your chest open and your shoulder down.|Hold, then swap arms and repeat.

Attach a rope handle to a high pulley and kneel down facing away from the machine.|Hold the rope handle with both hands and place it behind your head, keeping your elbows out to the sides.|Keeping your hips stationary, flex your waist and crunch your torso down towards your thighs.|Pause for a moment at the bottom, then slowly return to the starting position.|Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Attach a straight bar to a low pulley and stand close to the stack.|Hold the bar with an overhand grip in front of your thighs.|Keep your back straight and your abs tight.|Pull the bar up to shoulder height, leading with your elbows.|Lower the bar under control back to your thighs.

Sit on the edge of a sturdy chair and grip the front with both hands.|Slide your hips off the seat with your legs out in front.|Bend your elbows to lower your hips towards the floor.|Stop when your upper arms are level with the seat.|Push back up until your arms are straight.

Sit on a bench with your feet flat on the floor and hold a barbell with an underhand grip, hands shoulder-width apart.|Rest your upper arms against your inner thighs, just above your knees, and let the barbell hang down in front of you.|Keeping your upper arms stationary, exhale and curl the barbell up towards your shoulders, contracting your biceps.|Hold the contracted position for a brief pause, then inhale and slowly lower the barbell back down to the starting position.|Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

column2: Dumbbell Seated One Leg Calf Raise
column9: Sit on a bench with the ball of one foot on a low step and your heel hanging off.|Rest a dumbbell on top of that knee and hold it in place.|Push through the ball of your foot to raise your heel as high as you can.|Pause at the top and squeeze your calf.|Lower your heel slowly below the step and switch legs after the set.

Kneel on a pad with your ankles held down by a partner or a heavy anchor.|Loop a band around your chest and anchor it above and behind you.|Keep your hips straight so your body makes one line from knees to shoulders.|Lower yourself forward as slowly as you can and let your hands catch you.|Push yourself back up with your arms and reset for the next rep.

Lie on your side next to a bench, propped on your forearm with your elbow directly under your shoulder.|Rest the inside of your top leg on the bench, at the knee to make it easier or at the ankle to make it harder, with your bottom leg on the floor under it.|Brace your core and lift your hips until your body forms a straight line from head to feet.|Press your top leg down into the bench and raise your bottom leg until it touches the underside of the bench.|Lower the bottom leg towards the floor with control, keeping your hips up, and switch sides after the set.

Start by hanging from a pull-up bar with your palms facing away from you and your arms fully extended.|Retract your shoulder blades by pulling them down and back.|Engage your back muscles and pull your body up towards the bar, focusing on squeezing your shoulder blades together.|Pause for a moment at the top of the movement, then slowly lower your body back down to the starting position.|Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Put a small plate or wedge under both heels.|Hold a dumbbell against your chest with both hands.|Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart on the wedge.|Squat straight down, keeping your torso upright.|Push through your feet to stand back up.

Put a band around your legs, just above the knees or at the ankles.|Bend your knees slightly and push them out against the band.|Step sideways without letting your feet come together.|Take several steps in one direction.|Walk back the other way to finish the set.

Sit on the floor with your legs straight and a band around your feet.|Hold an end of the band in each hand with your arms out.|Sit tall with your chest up.|Pull your elbows back until your hands reach your ribs.|Straighten your arms slowly against the band.

Lie on a decline bench with your feet secured and your head lower than your hips.|Hold a dumbbell in each hand with your palms facing each other and your arms extended above your chest.|Lower the dumbbells out to the sides in a wide arc until you feel a stretch in your chest.|Pause for a moment, then squeeze your chest muscles to bring the dumbbells back to the starting position.|Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Stand side-on to a cable machine set at chest height.|Hold the handle with both hands and press it straight out.|Lock your arms and keep them level with your sternum.|Resist the cable pulling your torso around.|Hold the position, then swap sides and repeat.

Stand or sit up tall with your shoulders relaxed.|Bring one straight arm across your chest.|Hook the other forearm under it and pull it closer.|Keep the shoulder down instead of shrugging it.|Hold the stretch, then change arms.

Sit on the floor with your hands behind you and your knees bent.|Lift your hips so only your hands and feet touch the ground.|Walk forward by moving an opposite hand and foot together.|Keep your hips up the whole time.|Walk back the other way to finish the set.

Stand up straight with your feet shoulder-width apart and hold a barbell with an underhand grip, hands close together.|Keep your elbows close to your torso and your upper arms stationary throughout the movement.|Exhale as you curl the weights while contracting your biceps. Continue to raise the bar until your biceps are fully contracted and the bar is at shoulder level.|Hold the contracted position for a brief pause as you squeeze your biceps.|Inhale as you slowly begin to bring the barbell back to the starting position.

Stand on the edge of a step or platform with your heels hanging off and your toes on the step.|Hold a dumbbell in one hand and place your other hand on a wall or railing for support.|Raise your heel as high as possible, lifting your body up onto your toes.|Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your heel back down below the step.|Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch to the other leg.

Start by standing with your feet shoulder-width apart and the barbell resting on your upper back.|Keeping your back straight and your core engaged, hinge forward at the hips, pushing your buttocks back as if you were trying to touch the wall behind you with your glutes.|Lower your torso until it is parallel to the ground, feeling a stretch in your hamstrings.|Pause for a moment, then return to the starting position by squeezing your glutes and pushing your hips forward.|Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Get into a side plank on your forearm with your feet stacked.|Line up your elbow under your shoulder.|Lower your hip towards the floor without touching it.|Drive your hip back up until your body is straight again.|Finish the reps on one side before swapping.

Stand tall with your feet hip-width apart.|Run on the spot, driving one knee up at a time.|Bring each knee up to hip height.|Land softly on the balls of your feet.|Pump your arms in time with your legs.

Loop a band around your ankles and get into a quarter squat.|Keep tension on the band by pushing your knees out.|Step forward and out at a diagonal with one foot.|Repeat with the other foot, staying low.|Walk forwards, then walk backwards the same way.

Adjust the cable pulldown machine so that the seat is at a comfortable height and the knee pad is secured.|Sit on the seat with your back straight and your feet flat on the ground.|Grasp the cable bar with an overhand grip, slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.|Lean back slightly and engage your core.|Pull the cable bar down towards your chest, squeezing your shoulder blades together.

Lie flat on a bench with a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing each other.|Extend your arms straight up over your chest, with a slight bend in your elbows.|Keeping a slight bend in your elbows, lower your arms out to the sides in a wide arc until you feel a stretch in your chest.|Pause for a moment, then reverse the movement and bring the dumbbells back up to the starting position.|Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Set a pulley high and stand side-on to it with your feet wide.|Grab the handle with both hands above the shoulder nearest the stack.|Keep your arms long and your core braced.|Pull the handle down and across your body towards the opposite knee, turning your hips and back foot.|Return the handle slowly to the top and switch sides after the set.

Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand with your palms facing your thighs.|Keeping your arms straight, exhale and lift the dumbbells in front of you until they are at shoulder level.|Pause for a moment at the top, then inhale and slowly lower the dumbbells back down to the starting position.|Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Lie on a decline bench with your head lower than your feet and hold a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing each other.|Extend your arms fully, keeping your elbows close to your head.|Lower the dumbbells slowly behind your head, bending your elbows.|Pause for a moment, then raise the dumbbells back to the starting position.|Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Stand facing the cable machine with your feet shoulder-width apart.|Grasp the cable attachment with an underhand grip, palms facing up.|Keep your elbows close to your sides and your upper arms stationary.|Exhale and curl the cable attachment towards your shoulders, contracting your biceps.|Pause for a moment at the top of the movement, squeezing your biceps.

Adjust the seat of the leg press machine so that your knees are slightly bent when your feet are on the footplate.|Sit on the machine with your back against the backrest and your feet flat on the footplate, shoulder-width apart.|Place your toes and the balls of your feet on the footplate, keeping your heels off the edge.|Release the safety handles and push the footplate away from you by extending your knees.|Once your knees are fully extended, slowly lower your heels by flexing your calves.

Stand on one leg with a soft bend in that knee.|Hinge forward at the hip and let the free leg rise straight behind you.|Reach your hands towards the floor and keep your hips level.|Stop when your torso and back leg are almost parallel to the floor.|Squeeze the glute to stand back up without touching the free foot down.

Sit on a stability ball with your feet shoulder-width apart and flat on the ground.|Hold a weight in one hand and place your other hand on your hip.|Engage your core and slowly bend sideways towards the weighted side, keeping your back straight.|Pause for a moment at the bottom, then slowly return to the starting position.|Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch sides.

Sit in the machine with the pads on the inside of your knees.|Start with your legs open and your back against the seat.|Squeeze your knees together against the resistance.|Hold for a second when your legs meet.|Let the pads push your knees apart slowly.

Sit on a bench with a band looped above your knees.|Plant your feet and keep your back straight.|Push your knees apart against the band.|Hold the open position for a second.|Let your knees come back together slowly.

Sit on the cable row machine with your feet flat on the footrests and your knees slightly bent.|Grasp the handles with an overhand grip, keeping your back straight and your shoulders relaxed.|Pull the handles towards your body, squeezing your shoulder blades together.|Pause for a moment at the peak of the movement, then slowly release the handles back to the starting position.|Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Adjust the seat so the handles line up with your upper chest.|Sit with your back against the pad and grab both handles.|Press the handles forward and up until your arms are almost straight.|Stop just short of locking your elbows.|Let the handles come back slowly to your upper chest.

Get into the captain's chair with your forearms on the pads.|Let your legs hang straight with your back against the pad.|Lift both knees towards your chest without swinging.|Curl your hips up slightly at the top of the rep.|Lower your legs slowly until they hang straight again.

Lie on a flat bench with a dumbbell in each hand.|Raise the dumbbells straight over your shoulders.|Keep your upper arms still for the whole set.|Bend your elbows to lower the dumbbells beside your head.|Straighten your arms to bring the dumbbells back up.

Stand upright with your feet shoulder-width apart and a slight bend in your knees.|Hold the cable rope attachment with an underhand grip, palms facing each other, and your arms fully extended.|Keeping your upper arms stationary, exhale and curl the weights while contracting your biceps.|Continue to raise the cable rope attachment until your biceps are fully contracted and the rope is at shoulder level.|Hold the contracted position for a brief pause as you squeeze your biceps.

Adjust the machine to your height and stand with your feet shoulder-width apart.|Place your shoulders under the pads and hold onto the handles for stability.|Raise your heels as high as possible by extending your ankles.|Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your heels back down to the starting position.|Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Lie face down on a flat bench with your knees just off the end.|Have a partner place a dumbbell between your feet and squeeze it tight.|Curl your heels towards your glutes, lifting the dumbbell.|Keep your hips pressed into the bench at the top.|Lower the dumbbell slowly until your legs are almost straight.

Stand with your feet together and your arms at your sides.|Jump your feet out wide while you raise your arms overhead.|Land softly with your knees slightly bent.|Jump back to bring your feet together and your arms down.|Keep a steady rhythm for the whole set.

Loop a band around both ankles and stand tall.|Hold a wall or a rack for balance.|Lift one leg straight out to the side against the band.|Keep your torso upright and your hips square.|Bring the leg back in slowly and repeat.

Get on all fours with your hands under your shoulders.|Breathe out and round your back, tucking your chin and hips.|Breathe in and drop your belly, lifting your chest and tailbone.|Move slowly between the two positions.|Let your breathing set the pace.

Sit back on a bench set to about 45 degrees with a dumbbell in each hand.|Hold the dumbbells beside your chest with your palms facing each other.|Keep your feet flat and your back against the bench.|Press the dumbbells up until your arms are straight.|Lower them slowly back to the sides of your chest.

Lie flat on your back with your knees bent and feet flat on the ground.|Place your hands behind your head with your elbows pointing outwards.|Engage your abs and lift your shoulders off the ground, curling forward towards your knees.|Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your shoulders back down to the starting position.|Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and hold a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing your body.|Bend your knees slightly and hinge forward at the hips, keeping your back straight and core engaged.|Raise your arms out to the sides, keeping a slight bend in your elbows, until they are parallel to the floor.|Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your arms back down to the starting position.|Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and hold a dumbbell in one hand.|Raise the dumbbell overhead, keeping your arm straight.|Bend your elbow and lower the dumbbell behind your head, keeping your upper arm stationary.|Extend your arm back up to the starting position.|Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Attach a straight bar to a low pulley cable machine.|Lie face up on a flat bench with your feet flat on the ground.|Grasp the bar with an underhand grip, hands shoulder-width apart.|Extend your arms fully, keeping your elbows close to your sides.|Keeping your upper arms stationary, exhale and curl the bar up towards your shoulders.

Stand with your feet hip-width apart and place your hands on a wall or sturdy object for balance.|Lift one foot off the ground and balance on the other foot.|Slowly raise your heel off the ground, lifting your body up onto the ball of your foot.|Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your heel back down to the starting position.|Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch legs and repeat.

Wedge one end of a barbell into a landmine holder and load the other end.|Stand facing the bar and hold the loaded end with both hands.|Keep your back flat and your knees slightly bent.|Push your hips back and let the bar travel down your thighs.|Drive your hips forward to stand up and squeeze your glutes.

Hold the kettlebell by the horns against your chest, elbows tucked in.|Set your feet shoulder-width apart with your toes turned out slightly.|Sit down between your heels, keeping your chest tall and the bell close.|Go as deep as your hips allow without your lower back rounding.|Drive through the floor to stand back up.

Sit on a bench with your back against the bench and your feet flat on the ground.|Place your hands on the bench for support.|Engage your glutes and hamstrings, then lift your hips off the bench until your body forms a straight line from your knees to your shoulders.|Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your hips back down to the starting position.|Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Kneel on the floor and sit back onto your heels.|Open your knees a little wider than your hips.|Walk your hands forward and rest your forehead on the floor.|Let your chest sink towards the ground.|Breathe slowly and hold the position.

Stand tall with a dumbbell in each hand in front of your thighs.|Turn your palms towards your body and keep your abs tight.|Raise the dumbbells towards your shoulders by lifting your elbows out to the sides.|Stop when your elbows reach shoulder height.|Lower the dumbbells slowly back to your thighs.

Put one knee and the same-side hand on a bench with your back flat.|Hold a dumbbell in the other hand with your upper arm tucked against your side.|Start with your elbow bent to 90 degrees.|Straighten your arm behind you until it is fully extended.|Bend the elbow slowly back to 90 degrees and switch arms after the set.

Attach a straight bar to a low pulley cable machine.|Lie face up on a flat bench with your feet flat on the ground.|Grasp the bar with an underhand grip, hands shoulder-width apart.|Extend your arms fully, keeping your elbows close to your sides.|Keeping your upper arms stationary, curl the bar towards your chest by contracting your biceps.

Set the Smith bar at shoulder height and step under it.|Rest the bar across your upper back and stand with the balls of your feet on a low step.|Unlock the bar and let your heels hang off the edge.|Rise up onto your toes as high as you can.|Lower your heels slowly below the step.

Lie on your back with your knees bent and lift your hips into a bridge.|Keep your hips up for the whole exercise.|Walk your heels out step by step until your legs are almost straight.|Walk them back in the same way.|Stop if your hips start to drop towards the floor.

Hold the kettlebell against your chest in the goblet position.|Step one foot back and lower until the back knee nearly touches the floor.|Keep your front shin vertical and your torso upright.|Push through the front foot to return to standing.|Alternate legs or finish one side first.

Sit on the floor and bring the soles of your feet together.|Pull your heels in towards your body.|Hold your feet with both hands and sit up tall.|Let your knees fall out towards the floor.|Lean forward gently and hold the stretch.

Attach a close-grip handle to the lat pulldown and sit with your thighs under the pad.|Take the handle with both palms facing each other.|Lean back slightly and keep your chest up.|Pull the handle down to your upper chest, driving your elbows to your sides.|Let the handle rise slowly until your arms are fully stretched.

Kneel on the floor and put your hands under your shoulders.|Walk your hands forward until your body forms a straight line from head to knees.|Lower your chest towards the floor with your elbows tucked.|Stop when your chest is a fist away from the ground.|Push back up without letting your hips sag.

Lie on your back with your hands under your hips.|Lift both legs a few centimetres off the floor.|Press your lower back down into the ground.|Kick your legs up and down in small alternating movements.|Keep your legs straight and your core tight.

Adjust the seat height and position yourself on the machine with your back against the backrest.|Grasp the handles with an overhand grip and position your hands at shoulder level.|Push the handles upward until your arms are fully extended, but do not lock your elbows.|Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower the handles back down to the starting position.|Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Hold one kettlebell by the horns with both hands overhead.|Keep your elbows pointing forward and close to your head.|Bend at the elbows to lower the bell behind your head.|Stop when you feel the stretch in your triceps.|Straighten your arms to press it back up.

Place a preacher bench in front of a low pulley with a short bar.|Rest your upper arms on the pad and hold the bar with your palms up.|Start with your arms fully straight.|Curl the bar up towards your head.|Lower it slowly until your arms are straight again.

Stand facing a wall and put both hands on it.|Step one foot back and keep that leg straight.|Press the back heel into the floor.|Lean towards the wall until you feel the calf stretch.|Hold, then swap legs.

Lie on your back with your heels in the rings, set just off the floor.|Lift your hips so your body makes one line from shoulders to heels.|Pull your heels towards your backside by bending your knees.|Keep your hips high the whole way, then straighten your legs slowly.|Drop your hips to the floor to rest between sets.

Hold the loaded end of a landmine bar against your chest with both hands.|Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart.|Sit down between your hips, letting the bar guide you.|Go down until your thighs are parallel to the floor.|Push the floor away to stand back up.

Stand facing away from the cable machine with your feet shoulder-width apart.|Grab the rope attachment with both hands and step forward, creating tension in the cable.|Bend at the hips and lower your upper body until it is parallel to the ground, keeping your back straight.|Engage your glutes and hamstrings to pull your body back up to the starting position.|Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Set an incline bench to a 45-degree angle and sit on it with a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing inwards.|Lean forward slightly and let your arms hang straight down, keeping a slight bend in your elbows.|Raise your arms out to the sides and up in a Y shape until they are parallel to the ground.|Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your arms back down to the starting position.|Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Adjust the seat height and position yourself on the machine with your feet flat on the ground.|Grasp the handles with an overhand grip and position your hands at chest level.|Push the handles forward until your arms are fully extended, keeping your elbows slightly bent.|Pause for a moment, then slowly bring the handles back towards your chest, maintaining control throughout the movement.|Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Start standing with your feet hip-width apart.|Drop into a squat and place both hands on the floor.|Jump your feet back into a plank position.|Jump them straight back in towards your hands.|Stand up tall and go into the next rep.

Lie face down on a raised bench with a dumbbell in each hand.|Let your arms hang below the bench with your elbows slightly bent.|Keep your toes on the floor to stay steady.|Raise the dumbbells out to the sides up to shoulder height.|Lower them slowly until your arms hang down again.

Adjust the seat so your elbows line up with the machine's pivot.|Rest your upper arms on the pad and grab the handles.|Keep your upper arms pressed into the pad.|Push the handles down until your arms are straight.|Let the handles come back up slowly until your elbows are fully bent.

Stand tall with a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing your body.|Keep your elbows close to your sides.|Curl one dumbbell up and across towards the opposite shoulder.|Keep your palm facing in without twisting the wrist.|Lower it slowly and repeat with the other arm.

Stand on a raised platform with your toes on the edge and your heels hanging off.|Hold onto a stable object for support.|Raise your heels as high as possible by extending your ankles.|Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your heels back down to the starting position.|Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Lie on your back and loop a towel around the sole of one foot.|Hold an end of the towel in each hand.|Straighten that leg and pull it up towards the ceiling.|Stop when you feel a stretch along the back of the thigh and hold.|Lower the leg slowly and switch sides.

Get into an athletic stance with your knees bent and your chest up.|Push off one foot to slide sideways.|Take quick steps without crossing your feet.|Stay low and keep your weight on the balls of your feet.|Shuffle back in the other direction.

Strap a cable cuff around the ankle furthest from the machine.|Hold the frame for balance and stand tall.|Lift the working leg out to the side, keeping it straight.|Stop when you feel the side of your glute working.|Bring the leg back down slowly without letting the stack rest.

Sit in the lateral raise machine with the pads against your outer arms.|Set the seat so the pivot lines up with your shoulders.|Push your arms out and up until they reach shoulder height.|Keep your neck relaxed and your traps out of the movement.|Lower the pads slowly back to your sides.

Attach a straight bar to a high pulley and face the stack.|Hold the bar with your palms facing up.|Pin your elbows to your sides.|Push the bar down towards your thighs until your arms are straight.|Let the bar rise slowly without moving your elbows.

Sit on a preacher bench with a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing your torso and arms fully extended.|Keep your upper arms stationary and exhale as you curl the weights while contracting your biceps.|Continue to raise the dumbbells until your biceps are fully contracted and the dumbbells are at shoulder level.|Hold the contracted position for a brief pause as you squeeze your biceps.|Inhale and slowly begin to lower the dumbbells back to the starting position.

Stand on a low box or step on one leg.|Let the other leg hang just off the edge.|Bend your standing knee slowly to lower the free heel towards the floor.|Tap the floor lightly without shifting your weight onto it.|Straighten your standing leg to rise back up and switch legs after the set.

Attach a cable to a low pulley and stand facing away from the machine.|Place the cable around your ankle and stand with your feet shoulder-width apart.|Keep your core engaged and your back straight throughout the exercise.|Slowly extend your leg straight back, squeezing your glutes at the top of the movement.|Pause for a moment, then return to the starting position.

Sit on the pec deck with your back flat against the pad and your feet planted.|Set the handles so your upper arms sit level with your shoulders.|Grab both handles with a light bend in your elbows.|Squeeze your chest to bring the handles together in front of you.|Open your arms back slowly until you feel a stretch across your chest.

Stand tall and bend forward to put your hands on the floor.|Walk your hands out until you reach a push-up position.|Hold there for a moment with your core tight.|Walk your feet up towards your hands with your legs as straight as you can.|Stand back up and repeat.

Adjust the seat height and position yourself on the machine with your chest against the pad and your feet flat on the floor.|Grasp the handles with an overhand grip and keep your arms slightly bent.|Exhale and squeeze your shoulder blades together as you pull the handles back and outward, away from your body.|Pause for a moment at the peak contraction, then inhale and slowly return to the starting position.|Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Attach a rope to a high pulley and take an end in each hand.|Stand tall with your elbows pinned to your sides.|Push the rope down until your arms are straight.|Spread the ends of the rope apart at the bottom and squeeze your triceps.|Let the rope rise back to chest height without moving your elbows.

Sit on a preacher bench with a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing up.|Rest your upper arms on the pad of the preacher bench, allowing your arms to fully extend.|Keeping your upper arms stationary, exhale and curl the dumbbell in your right hand as you contract your biceps.|Continue to curl the dumbbell until your biceps are fully contracted and the dumbbell is at shoulder level.|Pause for a moment, then inhale and slowly lower the dumbbell back to the starting position.

Lie on your side with your knees bent and your feet stacked.|Rest your head on your bottom arm and keep your hips still.|Open the top knee towards the ceiling, keeping your feet together.|Stop before your hips start to roll back.|Close the knee slowly and repeat.

Hinge forward with one hand braced on a bench or your thigh.|Let the kettlebell hang at full stretch from the other hand.|Pull the bell to your hip, leading with the elbow.|Squeeze the shoulder blade at the top without twisting your torso.|Lower it slowly and repeat, then swap sides.

Stand with your feet together and your arms straight out to the sides.|Jump your feet apart while you clap your hands in front of your chest.|Open your arms wide again as you jump your feet back together.|Keep your arms at shoulder height the whole time.|Repeat at a steady pace.

Lie on your back with your legs straight and your hands by your hips.|Press your lower back into the floor.|Lift both legs until they point at the ceiling.|Lower them slowly without touching the ground.|Stop the descent as soon as your back starts to arch.
